answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked until its actions survive a challenge window; a verifier can submit evidence of duplicate control, and proven Sybils forfeit their bonds. This does not make identities scarce by itself: it makes attacks costly when fake agents must earn rewards or influence decisions. An attacker has to fund many deposits and risk losing them, while coordinating the accounts without triggering detection. The basalt ledger may record claims, a nebula of aliases can still form, but each exposed duplicate shifts the delta toward losses.
